title: 2026-10-29_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_5bc
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is a modular Linux backdoor that can install itself with or without root privileges. Your goal is to identify and analyze the suspicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the affected systems.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes.
Analyze network traffic for signs of command-and-control (C2) communication.
Contain and eradicate the malware to prevent further compromise.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is a modular Linux backdoor that can install itself with or without root privileges. Your goal is to identify and analyze the suspicious activity, contain the threat, and remove the malware from the affected systems.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Sofacy2023!
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials. Username: investigator, Password: Sofacy2023!

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the `target` host. Investigate the host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the `systemctl` command to list all running services. Look for any services that appear unusual or unauthorized. The service name is `bkd`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to see all running services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine which network port it is using for communication. This information is crucial for containing the threat.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used by the suspicious service, you can use the `ss` or `netstat` command to list all network connections. Look for the port associated with the `bkd` service. The C2 port number is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate the network connections associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss` or `netstat` command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `ss -tulnp` to see all network connections.

levels.title: Process Termination
levels.content: To prevent further communication with the command-and-control server, you need to stop the malicious process. Identify and terminate the process associated with the suspicious service.
levels.solution: To terminate the malicious process, you can use the `kill` command. First, identify the process ID (PID) of the `ncat` process using the `ps` or `pgrep` command. Then, use the `kill` command to terminate the process. The process name is `ncat`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use process management commands to identify and terminate the malicious process.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ps` or `pgrep` command to identify the process ID (PID) of the `ncat` process.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command `ps aux | grep ncat` to identify the process ID (PID) of the `ncat` process.
